title: Compact schema watchdog for interleaved toolcalls
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: streaming responses that interleave tool/function call tokens with JSON payloads frequently trigger strict JSON mode decoders to fail or fall back to expensive retries. We need a lightweight, deterministic watchdog test harness and telemetry surface that simulates realistic interleaving and verifies our constrained-decoding fallback behaviors without requiring full heavyweight fuzz suites.

Goal: implement a compact test harness + set of canonical scenarios that 1) exercise interleaved toolcall insertion mid-object, 2) measure decoder false positive/negative rates under temperature/noise, and 3) validate graceful fallbacks (relaxed parse/repair prompt) within SLOs. Deliver a telemetry dashboard and automated CI gate that flags regressions in schema adherence for streaming flows that include tool/function tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can simulate 10 canonical interleaved scenarios (see test_plan) against at least three model families and report pass/fail
False-positive detection rate (flagging valid output as invalid) <= 1% on baseline models at temperature <= 0.2
Fallback path (relaxed-parse + constrained-decoder-retry) restores valid JSON for >= 95% of recoverable cases within 2s median additional latency
CI job added that runs on main for all PRs touching streaming decoders and fails on regression above thresholds
Telemetry events emitted for: schema_violation_detected, fallback_invoked, fallback_success, parse_latency_ms
test_plan: Scenario A: tool-call token inserted in the middle of an object property ("tool_call_start" token breaks JSON)
Scenario B: truncated stream (sudden EOF) with partial array payload and subsequent toolcall tokens
Scenario C: repeated small interleaved toolcalls between array elements (simulates agent chatter)
Scenario D: noise tokens injected (sampling=0.7) inside numeric fields to simulate hallucination noise
Scenario E: long KV cache warmup (long prefix) and late toolcall insertion to stress incremental decoder state
Scenario F: multi-tool calls where tool returns serialized JSON immediately after streaming answer chunk
Scenario G: benign extra fields added by model (schema relaxation path should accept if allowed), and flagged otherwise
Scenario H: cross-model compatibility check (quantized variants behave consistently vs float)
observability_requirements: Expose event counts and 95th/99th parse_latency_ms in Console per-route dashboard
Tag events with model, deployment_type (hosted/dedicated/private), and sampling parameters
Provide linkable run artifacts (raw streams + golden JSON) for failed cases
ci_integration: New CI job linear/harness/stream-watchdog that runs the 10-scenario suite in ~30m on pre-commit runners
Job fails when fallback_success_rate < 95% or false_positive_rate > 1%
Artifacts uploaded to S3 with prefixes: /ci/stream-watchdog/{run_id}
dependencies_notes: Needs constrained-decoder shims from ENG-412356 and streaming telemetry primitives from ENG-14266. Also coordinate with SRE for CI GPU quota slice.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: CI runtime increases due to model matrix. Mitigation: sample smaller matrix on PRs and run full matrix nightly.
Risk: False negatives where watchdog misses subtle schema drift. Mitigation: pair with periodic fuzzing jobs and watchlist prompts.
Risk: Model-specific tokenization artifacts cause non-deterministic failures. Mitigation: normalize stream tokens and include synthetic control model to catch infra flakes.

notes: This is intentionally a compact, reviewable harness intended to catch regressions early in PRs. It is not a replacement for the large fuzzing suites but should serve as a fast gate for structured-output + tool-calling paths.
